questions.title: The defining feature of connective tissue
questions.question: Which of the following is considered a main characteristic feature of connective tissue?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Avascularity is a feature of epithelium (which is nourished by diffusion from underlying connective tissue), not connective tissue itself, which is generally well vascularised.
explanations.B: Correct. Connective tissue is defined by having relatively few cells widely separated by an abundant extracellular matrix — ground substance plus fibres — that the cells themselves secrete. This is the opposite arrangement from epithelium, whose cells sit closely packed with minimal matrix between them. The sheer bulk of matrix relative to cells is what a histology slide of connective tissue shows at a glance.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Closely packed cells with minimal intervening material describe epithelium, not connective tissue.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Resting on a basement membrane is a feature of epithelium, which sits on this specialised layer separating it from the underlying connective tissue.

questions.learning_objective: Name an abundant extracellular matrix as connective tissue's defining feature.
